organizations.csv: c01 is not unique (999 distinct over 1030 rows) and has 1.3% nulls, but organization.organization_id must be present and unique; the integrator will need to deduplicate/synthesize ids at validation.
Rule 2 (dormant = inactive if no activity in last 18 months) cannot be enforced from this dataset alone; after activities are loaded, some organizations’ lifecycle_status may need to be overridden.

Country disambiguation per Rule 5: when c06='CA' and c05 is blank/unrecognized, we will default billing_country to 'CA' (Canada). If additional metadata (e.g., record created date) becomes available, we could refine this further.
c07 contains many URLs without a scheme and some placeholders; we will normalize scheme, and invalid/placeholder values can be nulled during validation per integrator policy.
c12 includes some malformed emails; contact.email is required in the contact entity. Lowercasing is handled here; invalid formats will be addressed in validation.
‘Platinum’ in c09 will be treated as ‘Gold’ per Rule 3 if Option A is chosen in the clarification.
contacts.csv: contact.email is required; 106 emails are malformed and 66 normalize to duplicates (case-insensitive). These will need remediation or exceptions at validation to satisfy the uniqueness-within-organization rule.
Phone numbers have e164_count = 0 and 88 malformed; E.164 normalization is required. The proposal assumes NANP (+1) for 10-digit numbers—pending customer confirmation.

The full name in c17 will be used to populate both contact.first_name (targeted) and contact.last_name (from the same split). Edge cases with middle names/suffixes will follow the 'last token = last_name' rule; any single-token names will leave first_name blank for validation handling.

c20 role mapping follows Rule 13 where defined. Unspecified categories (e.g., 'Purchasing', 'Ops Manager', possibly 'Main') are proposed as shown and need confirmation. Where c21 is blank, per Rule 13 we plan to infer is_primary = true when c20 ∈ {'Primary','CEO','Owner'}, subject to customer confirmation.

c01 must be confirmed. If it is not the organization key, contacts will lack a reference to their organization and cannot be loaded (contact.organization_id is required). If it is a ZIP/postal code, there is no destination in the core schema and it will be dropped.
c22 contains 8 future dates; understanding what this field represents is necessary before considering any cross-entity mapping.
Role is optional in Meridian and defaults to 'other'; c20 has ~15.8% nulls, which will default to 'other' if not provided.
subscriptions.json: Rule 11 requires excluding trial subscriptions older than 90 days from migration; implement a filter during validation using the available date(s) (likely start_date) and status = trial.
41 rows have null seats in c28 while subscription.seats is required; resolution (defaulting, backfill, or exclusion) should be handled at validation.
Ensure the organization keys used in this file (c01 cast to string) match exactly the organization.organization_id values loaded from the organizations dataset to satisfy cross-record rules.
Input dates in c29 and c30 use mixed formats; the specified parsing should normalize them to YYYY-MM-DD. Renewal date must be after start date per target constraint.
c31 contains mixed numeric/text currency formats; the described normalization removes symbols/codes and keeps numeric amounts. No currency conversion should be applied even when c32 = CAD (rule 12).
activity.csv: activity.organization_id (c01) must reference an existing organization; ensure the organization migration uses the same IDs (string form of the 10xxx numbers) so lookups succeed.
c36 contains a mix of integers, numeric text, and floats and also 650 placeholders; parsing/invalid handling for out-of-pattern values will be addressed at validation by the engineer.
The datetime field c35 includes formats without timezone information; we’ve asked for the customer’s timezone assumption. No further data-quality defaults are chosen here.

rows.reason: Looks like a legacy account number: 5-digit+ integers, high distinctness, typical for an org key; organization_id is required and commonly holds the legacy id.
Non-null, highly distinct business-style names; this is the best fit for the organization’s display name.
Values are lifecycle states with case/typo variants (Active, Inactive, Prospect, Churned, On Hold, Closed). This aligns with lifecycle_status and Rule 6 for On Hold/Closed.
Compact industry/sector codes and NAICS-like digits (e.g., MFG, CONST, 31) match the industry enum.
Two-letter codes and full names like AB, GA, Colorado indicate state/province region.
Country codes/names (US, USA, U.S., Canada, CAN, MX, Mexico) align with billing_country, which requires ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; Rule 5 addresses 'CA' ambiguity.
URL-like values with many missing schemes are consistent with a website field.
Date field with mixed formats and some future dates could be customer_since or a subscription date; dataset provides two similar date columns (c08, c14).
Values are sales tiers (Gold, Silver, Bronze, Strategic, Platinum). Rule 3 says Strategic is a special designation; mapping tiers to operational priority is a business choice.
Large currency-like amounts (e.g., $7,050,000; 33450000) align with annual revenue.
Integer-like headcount values (22–3999, some as '899.0') match employee_count.
This looks like the primary contact’s email, and Rule 1 says the account-row primary_contact_email should be used to create/flag the primary contact.
Highly distinct two-word person-like strings suggest a contact name, likely tied to c12 for the primary contact, but this must be split across first and last name fields.
Second date column similar to c08 with some future dates; likely a subscription-related date rather than an org-level field, but unclear which.
Short categorical notes such as 'acquired by parent co' and 'renewal call scheduled' are good candidates for tags.
Unique, non-null identifier shaped like CT-000102 fits a stable contact-level id and matches the target id pattern.
Five-digit integers repeat across contacts (1046 distinct over 2279 rows), consistent with an account/organization key, but the values could also be postal codes.
Values look like personal names in 'Firstname Lastname' form; Meridian requires first_name and last_name separately.
Email-type column; contact.email is required and must be a valid email.
Phone-type column with North American-style formats; target requires E.164.
Free-text contact role; Rule 13 defines how several values map to Meridian roles.
Boolean flag likely indicating the primary contact; Rule 13 references an explicit primary flag.
A date is present but there is no contact-level date field in the catalog; the meaning is unclear from the data.
Boolean flag with Y/N values; Meridian’s core contact schema has no field for marketing opt-out or similar preferences.
Looks like a stable subscription identifier (e.g., SUB-00415), unique across all 1,003 rows and matches the subscription entity’s required id.
Highly likely to be the account/customer key referenced by each subscription (many subscriptions share the same value). Needed to link to organizations.
Plan names and synonyms that match the target enum; mapping governed by customer rules 7 and 8. 'Trial' requires a business decision for plan assignment.
Billing cadence values (monthly/annual and shorthands) with quarterly needing conversion per rule 9.
Subscription lifecycle states with synonyms; mapping covered by rule 10 for paused/expired and normalization for others.
Looks like seat counts (small set of typical seat numbers) required by subscription.seats.
One of two date columns; this one has minimal future dates, consistent with a start date.
The other date column; higher count of future dates is consistent with renewal/next billing date.
Monetary amounts per row consistent with monthly recurring revenue; rule 12 confirms amounts are monthly and CAD should be carried as-is in USD.
Target stores MRR in USD (subscription.mrr_usd). Per rule 12, CAD amounts are migrated as-is in USD; therefore the source currency code is not needed in the target.
Values look like stable activity identifiers (e.g., ACT-0003710), unique across all rows; this dataset is about activities.
Appears to be the account key (5-digit numbers reused across many rows), serving as the foreign key from activity to organization.
Category values align with the target activity kinds (invoice, payment, support_ticket, login, note). One extra value, 'Call', is not in the target enum and requires a decision.
Timestamps for when the activity happened; required datetime on activity.
Numeric amounts appear only on monetary activities; aligns with amount_usd on invoice/payment activities.
Currency code is always USD when present and the activity model only stores amount_usd; this field is redundant for the target and null on non-monetary rows.
Short phrases like 'payment received', 'portal login', and 'renewal discussion' fit the free-text activity description.
